subject: The send-only control-surface operations (MMC and MCU) and tracks.set_automation, against their own independent readbacks
question: The qualification sweep files these as measured walls. Is the wall the readback — a write that lands and cannot be confirmed — or does the write not land at all, and do they share a cause?

reverify.command: With Logic frontmost, park the playhead with logic_navigate.goto_bar {bar: 9}, read logic://transport/state, then call logic_transport.rewind and read it again; repeat for fast_forward. Then read logic://tracks[0].automationMode, call logic_tracks.set_automation {index: 0, mode: "touch"}, and read it again. Then read logic://mcu/state, call logic_tracks.arm {index: 0, enabled: true}, and read logic://tracks[0].isArmed. Finally call logic_midi.mmc_play and read logic://transport/state.isPlaying.
reverify.expected: All three answer State B with success true and verified false, and all three leave their independent field exactly where it was: position 9.1 before and after each transport call, automationMode "off" before and after. logic://mcu/state reports isConnected false; arm answers State B with verification_source mcu_led_echo and isArmed stays false; mmc_play answers State B send_only_no_readback and isPlaying stays false.

method: Each operation was driven through the release binary over stdio with Logic frontmost, with the independent resource read before and after and a settling pause between. Rewind was repeated twice to separate a single miss from a consistent one. Logic's frontmost status was asserted with System Events immediately before the transport pair, because a key-command path that silently needs focus would produce exactly this shape.

observations.control: logic_navigate.goto_bar {bar: 9} on the same fixture, same session
observations.note: the transport resource DOES report a playhead move when one happens, so the unchanged readings above are not a blind instrument
no source, no cache_age_sec, no data key — the resource carries no freshness envelope at all, so it cannot satisfy the gate whatever it says
State A here is correct and says nothing about the write path — nothing was asked for
the channel these operations verify through is not connected on this host

conclusion: For all of these the wall is the WRITE, not the readback, and most of them share one cause: the control-surface channels are not set up on this host. `transport.rewind`, `transport.fast_forward`, `midi.mmc_play` and `midi.mmc_stop` each leave as the same six-byte MMC message with `send_only_no_readback`, and the playhead stays at 9.1 across rewind twice and fast_forward while `isPlaying` stays false across mmc_play. `tracks.arm` verifies through `mcu_led_echo`, and `logic://mcu/state` reports `isConnected: false`, `registeredAsDevice: false` — so it is asking for confirmation from a surface that is not there, and `isArmed` does not move. That is not six walls; it is two unconfigured channels seen six times. `tracks.set_automation` is the one that stands apart: it takes the AX path, reports `automation_write_attempted: true`, and `automationMode` stays "off" — that one is unexplained. A control operation moves the transport field on the same fixture in the same session, so the instrument is not blind. The disposition for the six is a FIXTURE precondition rather than a recipe: a Phase-B cycle would stage, drive, read an unchanged field and refuse, which is already what they answer. Separately, the readback `logic://midi/ports` — declared for every `logic_midi` operation — carries no freshness envelope at all: no `source`, no `cache_age_sec`, no `data`. A previous note of mine said that resource answers null; it does not, it answers a port list, and the reason it cannot serve as evidence is the missing envelope rather than a missing answer.
limits: One fixture, one host, and the MMC finding is ABOUT THIS HOST: a Logic configured to obey MMC could see all four move. What is established here is that State B on these is not a readback gap, and that the four share a channel rather than four separate causes.

`set_automation` was driven with mode touch on track 0 only. Other modes and other tracks were not tried, so this does not establish that no mode ever lands — only that this one did not, while the operation reported the write attempted.
No attempt was made to find out WHY the AX automation write does not land. The record stops at the measurement; the cause is unmeasured and should not be guessed from it.

The product ships a consented one-time setup for the arm path (`system.setup_arm_key`), and this fixture has not run it. So `tracks.arm` is measured HERE as sending into an unconnected MCU channel; whether it lands after that setup is not measured and must not be inferred from this record either way.
